proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a version of every conditional law and fix \(x\) outside the common null set in the assumptions.  Write \(A_0=M_A(x)\), \(Z_0=M_Z(x)\), \(\gamma_j=\Gamma_Y(x)_{\cdot j}\), and \(\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\{\pi(x)\}\).  By conditional three-view independence,
\[
 S=A_0\Pi Z_0^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 T_u=A_0\Pi\operatorname{diag}(\gamma_{u1},\ldots,\gamma_{uK})Z_0^{\mathsf T}. \tag{1}
\]
The three rank assumptions and latent positivity make \(A_0,Z_0,\Pi\), and \(\Gamma_Y(x)\) invertible.  Hence \(S\) is invertible, and (1) gives the observable simultaneous-similarity family
\[
 T_uS^{-1}=A_0\operatorname{diag}(\gamma_{u1},\ldots,\gamma_{uK})A_0^{-1},\qquad u=1,\ldots,K. \tag{2}
\]
Because \(\Gamma_Y(x)\) is invertible, its columns are distinct and the diagonal matrices in (2) span the full diagonal algebra.  Consequently the common one-dimensional invariant subspaces of the algebra generated by \(\{T_uS^{-1}:u\le K\}\) are exactly \(\operatorname{span}(A_{0,\cdot j})\), \(j=1,\ldots,K\).  This proves recovery of the columns of \(A_0\) up to scaling and permutation.  Each column is a probability vector, so \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}A_{0,\cdot j}=1\) fixes its scale.

Put \(H=A_0^{-1}S=\Pi Z_0^{\mathsf T}\).  Since every column of \(Z_0\) sums to one,
\[
 H\mathbf 1_K=\Pi Z_0^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_K=\pi(x),
 \qquad
 Z_0^{\mathsf T}=\Pi^{-1}H. \tag{3}
\]
Thus (3) recovers \(\pi(x)\) and \(Z_0\) under the same permutation.  Finally, (1) yields
\[
 \operatorname{diag}(\gamma_{u1},\ldots,\gamma_{uK})
 =\Pi^{-1}A_0^{-1}T_u(Z_0^{\mathsf T})^{-1}, \tag{4}
\]
which recovers \(\Gamma_Y(x)\).

For the full outcome law, let \(p_A(y\mid x)\) be the \(K\)-vector whose \(a\)-th coordinate is the conditional joint density of \((Y,A=a)\) given \(X=x\).  Conditional independence gives
\[
 p_A(y\mid x)=A_0\Pi f(y\mid x),
 \qquad
 f(y\mid x)=\Pi^{-1}A_0^{-1}p_A(y\mid x) \quad \nu\text{-a.e.} \tag{5}
\]
All inversions in (2)--(5) are legitimate by the displayed rank and positivity assumptions.  Matrix inversion is Borel measurable on the nonsingular matrices.  The common eigenspaces in (2) can be selected measurably by choosing, from a fixed countable dense set of coefficient vectors, the first linear combination having distinct eigenvalues; such a combination exists because the columns of \(\Gamma_Y(x)\) are distinct.  The modal inequality assigns recovered column \(j\) to the unique row at which it has its maximum; its positive margin makes this assignment unique and measurable.  Hence (2)--(5) define an observed-law recovery map, not a definition of the causal target.

By (5), \(m_j(x)=E(Y\mid J=j,X=x)\).  Consistency gives
\[
 E\{Y(j)\mid J=j,X=x\}=E(Y\mid J=j,X=x)=m_j(x). \tag{6}
\]
Latent ignorability gives \(E\{Y(j)\mid J=j,X=x\}=E\{Y(j)\mid X=x\}\); latent positivity makes the conditioning event available.  Taking \(P_X\)-expectations in (6) proves
\[
 E\{Y(j)\}=E_P\{m_j(X)\}=\psi_j.
\]
Thus the causal estimand is equal to the recovered observed-law functional under the declared causal assumptions.

Fix a target class \(j\).  Invertibility of the two measurement matrices gives
\[
E\{a_j(A,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}=E\{z_j(Z,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}. \tag{25}
\]
Conditional independence then implies
\[
E(\phi_j\mid J=\ell,X)=m_j(X)-\psi_j. \tag{26}
\]
For a factorwise centered latent score, (25)--(26) give, term by term,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E(\phi_js_X)&=E[(m_j(X)-\psi_j)s_X(X)],\\
E(\phi_js_\pi)&=0,\\
E(\phi_js_Y)&=E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1(J=j)}{\pi_j(X)}\{Y-m_j(X)\}s_Y(Y,J,X)\right],\\
E(\phi_js_A)&=E(\phi_js_Z)=0.
\end{aligned} \tag{27}
\]
The first and third lines are exactly the derivatives of \(E_Pm_j(X)\) with respect to the \(X\)-marginal and the class-\(j\) outcome law; the other factor derivatives are zero.  The differential-score lifting theorem represents every observed DQM score by such a centered additive latent score.  Since \(\phi_j\) is observed measurable, iterated expectation and (27) prove the influence-function equation for every observed path.  Its mean is zero by (26), and bounded \(Y\), latent positivity, and the two inverse-matrix bounds give \(\phi_j\in L^2(P)\).

Appendix A.8 of Bian, Zhou, and Cui defines inverse features whose conditional expectations are latent-category indicators and multiplies two such features in its categorical influence function.  Setting its discount to zero and identifying reward with \(Y\), surrogate with \(A\), and the second proxy with \(Z\) gives exactly (25) and the displayed \(U_j\); this verifies the stated specialization independently of the preceding validity proof.

Use the notation of (1) in the proof of Theorem 1 and consider a derivative \((\dot\pi,\dot A_0,\dot Z_0,\dot\Gamma)\) satisfying the probability normalizations
\[
 \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot\pi=0,
 \qquad \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot A_0=0,
 \qquad \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot Z_0=0. \tag{7}
\]
We first prove injectivity of the derivative.  Suppose \(\dot S=0\) and \(\dot T_u=0\) for every \(u\).  Set
\[
 E_A=A_0^{-1}\dot A_0,\qquad E_Z=Z_0^{-1}\dot Z_0,
 \qquad p_j=\dot\pi_j/\pi_j.
\]
After multiplying \(\dot S=0\) on the left by \(A_0^{-1}\) and on the right by \(Z_0^{-\mathsf T}\), its \((r,s)\) entry for \(r\ne s\) is
\[
 (E_A)_{rs}\pi_s+\pi_r(E_Z)_{sr}=0. \tag{8}
\]
The same transformation of \(\dot T_u=0\), followed by (8), gives
\[
 (E_A)_{rs}\pi_s(\gamma_{us}-\gamma_{ur})=0,
 \qquad u=1,\ldots,K. \tag{9}
\]
Now
\[
 \|\gamma_s-\gamma_r\|_2
 =\|\Gamma_Y(e_s-e_r)\|_2
 \geq\sqrt2\,\varepsilon,
\]
so (9) implies \((E_A)_{rs}=0\), and (8) then implies \((E_Z)_{sr}=0\).  Thus both \(E_A\) and \(E_Z\) are diagonal.  Since \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}A_0=\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\), (7) gives \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}E_A=0\), hence \(E_A=0\); similarly \(E_Z=0\).  The diagonal part of \(\dot S=0\) then gives \(p=0\), and the diagonal part of each \(\dot T_u=0\) gives \(\dot\gamma_{ur}=0\).  The derivative is therefore injective on the normalized parameter tangent space.

The entries of \(A_0,Z_0\), and \(\pi\) lie in compact simplices, their least singular values and the entries of \(\pi\) are at least \(\varepsilon\), and \(|\gamma_{uj}|\leq\|h_0\|_\infty\).  On this compact set the derivative matrix is continuous.  The injectivity just proved says its least singular value is positive at every point; compactness makes the infimum positive.  Its reciprocal is bounded by the corrected \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\), which depends only on \(K,L,\varepsilon\), and the fixed feature envelope \(\|h_0\|_\infty\).  The Moore--Penrose inverse of this finite derivative is therefore the asserted right inverse on its image.  Its entries are Borel functions on the fixed-rank set.  The modal gap keeps the selected permutation locally constant, so the recovered derivatives respect the ordered labeling.  Dividing probability derivatives by their positive factor probabilities on supported atoms, and putting score zero on zero-probability atoms, produces the centered factor scores.

By the differential-score lifting theorem, every observed DQM score belongs to \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\); closure therefore gives \(\mathcal T\subseteq\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}\).  Conversely, at the stated two-sided pathwise-interior point, every bounded factorwise centered score generates an admissible product-factor DQM path.  Its observed score is its conditional expectation given \(O\), hence belongs to \(\mathcal T\).  Truncation and factorwise recentering make bounded scores dense in each factor \(L^2\) space, while conditional expectation is an \(L^2\) contraction.  Thus \(\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}\subseteq\mathcal T\), proving equality.

For the orthocomplement, let \(k\in L^2_0(P)\).  Orthogonality to all centered outcome-factor scores is equivalent, by conditional-expectation duality, to
\[
E(k\mid Y,J,X)=E(k\mid J,X). \tag{17}
\]
The analogous conditions for the two measurement factors replace \(Y\) in (17) by \(A\) and \(Z\).  Orthogonality to all centered propensity scores makes \(E(k\mid J,X)=E(k\mid X)\), and orthogonality to all marginal \(X\)-scores makes \(E(k\mid X)=E(k)=0\).  Hence orthogonality to the latent additive image implies the three displayed conditional-zero restrictions.  Conversely, any one of those restrictions implies \(E(k\mid J,X)=E(k\mid X)=0\); all three together make the inner product with every factor score zero by iterated expectation.  This proves the characterization.

Latent positivity and common support give \(w_j(y,x)>0\), hence \(W\) is invertible; cell positivity makes \(D\) invertible.  To prove that \(B\) has full column rank, suppose \(Bc=0\).  Reshaping this vector into a \(K\times K\) matrix gives
\[
M_A\operatorname{diag}(c)M_Z^{\mathsf T}=0.
\]
Multiplication by the two inverses, licensed by the surrogate and proxy rank assumptions, gives \(\operatorname{diag}(c)=0\), hence \(c=0\).

Bayes' rule and the conditional product factorization give, for \(r=(a,z)\),
\[
R_{rj}=\frac{w_jB_{rj}}{d_r},
\qquad R=D^{-1}BW,
\qquad R^{\mathsf T}D=WB^{\mathsf T},
\qquad R^{\mathsf T}DR=WB^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}BW. \tag{18}
\]
Let \(H=B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B\).  The established ranks make \(H\) and \(R^{\mathsf T}DR=WHW\) positive definite, so every displayed pseudoinverse is its ordinary inverse.  Therefore
\[
R(R^{\mathsf T}DR)^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}D
=D^{-1}BW(W^{-1}H^{-1}W^{-1})WB^{\mathsf T}
=D^{-1}BH^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}. \tag{19}
\]
This proves the equality of the two formulas for \(N_B\), without any equality restriction on the entries of \(w\).

Writing \(P_B=D^{-1}BH^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\), direct multiplication gives \(P_B^2=P_B\), \(P_B^{\mathsf T}D=DP_B\), and \(B^{\mathsf T}(I-P_B)=0\).  Hence
\[
N_B^2=N_B,\qquad N_B^{\mathsf T}D=DN_B,\qquad B^{\mathsf T}N_B=0. \tag{20}
\]
If \(B^{\mathsf T}v=0\), then \(N_Bv=v\), proving \(\operatorname{range}N_B=\ker B^{\mathsf T}\).  Also \(N_BD^{-1}B=0\), and both \(\operatorname{range}(D^{-1}B)\) and \(\ker N_B\) have dimension \(K\); thus they are equal.  Equation (18) and invertibility of \(W\) show that this space also equals \(\operatorname{range}R\).  In \(\mathfrak A_3\), the same proof uses ordinary inverses because its hypotheses give positive \(W,D\) and full-column-rank \(B\); (18)--(20) are the requested six exact symbolic identities for arbitrary positive nonconstant \(w\).

Fix \((y,x)\) and represent a function of the observed cells by \(k=(k_{az})\).  Conditional independence gives
\[
E(k\mid Y=y,J=j,X=x)=\sum_{a,z}B_{(a,z),j}(x)k_{az}, \tag{21}
\]
so all outcome restrictions are exactly \(B^{\mathsf T}k=0\).  Lemma 3A shows that \(N_B\) is idempotent, has this range, and is self-adjoint for \(\langle u,v\rangle_D=u^{\mathsf T}Dv\).  It is therefore the pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector.  Since \(R\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_{K^2}\), constants over the cells lie in \(\ker N_B\), so \(N_Bf_0\) has conditional mean zero given \((Y,X)\).

For a measurement coordinate \(r=(j,a)\), Bayes' rule gives
\[
E\{kR_{\cdot j}\mathbf 1(A=a)\mid X\}
=\pi_j E\{k\mathbf 1(A=a)\mid J=j,X\}. \tag{22}
\]
The corresponding identity with \(Z=z\) is identical.  Thus, after (21), the remaining two families of restrictions in Theorem 2 are precisely \(E(kc_r\mid X)=0\).  If \(k=N_Bk\), the \(D\)-self-adjointness of \(N_B\) gives
\[
E(kc_r\mid X)=E\{k(N_Bc_r)\mid X\}=E(kh_r\mid X). \tag{23}
\]

If \(v\in\ker G(X)\), then
\[
0=v^{\mathsf T}Gv=E\{(v^{\mathsf T}h)^2\mid X\},
\]
so \(v^{\mathsf T}h=0\) conditionally and \(v^{\mathsf T}b_{f_0}=0\).  Hence \(b_{f_0}\perp\ker G\), which for symmetric \(G\) is \(b_{f_0}\in\operatorname{range}G\).  Therefore \(GG^+b_{f_0}=b_{f_0}\), and
\[
E\{h(Qf_0)\mid X\}=b_{f_0}-GG^+b_{f_0}=0. \tag{24}
\]
Moreover every coordinate of \(h=N_Bc\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}N_B\), so \(Qf_0\) remains in that range.  Equations (21)--(24) and Theorem 2 show \(Qf_0\in\mathcal T^\perp\).

The two successive removed parts are orthogonal: \((I-N_B)f_0\) is pointwise orthogonal to \(\operatorname{range}N_B\), and \(h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_{f_0}\) is the conditional orthogonal projection of \(N_Bf_0\) onto the span of \(h\).  Hence, for every \(k\in\mathcal T^\perp\),
\[
E\{(f_0-Qf_0)k\}=0.
\]
The range characterized by the conditional-zero equations is an intersection of kernels of continuous conditional-expectation operators and is closed.  Thus \(Q\) is the asserted orthogonal projection.  The cell and Gram gaps bound its conditional coefficients and ensure measurability and integrability of the fixed-rank pseudoinverse.

Proposition 2 gives an influence-function vector \(\phi\).  Theorem 3 says that \(Q\phi\) is its orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal T^\perp\).  Consequently \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}=(I-Q)\phi\in\mathcal T\).  For every score \(s\in\mathcal T\), orthogonality gives
\[
E\{\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}s\}=E(\phi s)-E\{(Q\phi)s\}=\dot\psi(s),
\]
so \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\) remains an influence function.  If \(\widetilde\phi\in\mathcal T\) is another influence function, then \(E\{(\widetilde\phi-\phi^{\mathrm{eff}})s\}=0\) for all \(s\in\mathcal T\); its difference lies in both \(\mathcal T\) and \(\mathcal T^\perp\), hence is zero.  This proves uniqueness and identifies \(E(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\phi^{\mathrm{eff},\mathsf T})\) as the information bound.  The displayed construction uses a \(K^2\)-vector at each \((Y,X)\) and the Gram matrix of only \(2K^2\) residualized measurement coordinates.  No step introduces a basis in \(Y\), proving the dimension assertion.

By Proposition 10, in the binary restriction \(\operatorname{range}Q\) is the closed span of \(B_0h_0+B_1h_1\) with \(E(h_r\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}},X)=0\).  Every coordinate of \(V^\ell\) has this form because \(p_t^\ell\in\mathcal P_1^\ell\).  Hence \(\operatorname{span}(V^\ell)\subseteq\operatorname{range}Q\) whenever its denominators and Gram inverse are well defined.  Thus \(Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\) and \(Q\) are orthogonal projections onto nested subspaces, and
\[
Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}Q=Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}},\qquad
(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})^2=Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}. \tag{28}
\]
The orthogonal decomposition
\[
\phi-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\phi=(\phi-Q\phi)+(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi
\]
has orthogonal summands.  Taking outer-product expectations proves
\[
V_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}
=E[\{(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}\{(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}^{\mathsf T}]\succeq0. \tag{29}
\]
For a row vector \(c\), the quadratic form in (29) is the squared \(L^2(P)\)-norm of \(c^{\mathsf T}(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\), proving the strictness criterion.

Along a nested equal-width subsequence for which the cited Supplement S8.2 density assertion holds, the closed union of \(\operatorname{span}(V^\ell)\) is \(\operatorname{range}Q\).  Orthogonal projections onto increasing closed subspaces converge strongly to the projection onto the closure of their union: indeed, for any \(v\) in that union the projection error is eventually no larger than \(\|Q\phi-v\|_2\), and density makes this arbitrarily small.  Hence \(Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\phi\to Q\phi\) in \(L^2(P)\); (29) then gives covariance convergence.  All objects in this argument are binary.  The fixed-cell theorem for \(K\ge3\) is not obtained by this limit.

Fix \(c_j\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{adj}}\) and abbreviate \(v=v_j\), \(b=b_v\), and \(e=E\{(N_Bv)^2\mid X\}\).  The augmented Gram matrix is the Gram matrix of the coordinates \((h^{\mathsf T},N_Bv)^{\mathsf T}\), so adjoining its last coordinate increases rank by at most one.  Since \(b\in\operatorname{range}G\), block elimination with \(G^+\) gives
\[
\operatorname{rank}G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}
=\operatorname{rank}G+\mathbf 1\{e-b^{\mathsf T}G^+b>0\}. \tag{30}
\]
The last scalar is nonnegative because it is the conditional residual sum of squares,
\[
\Lambda_j(X)=E\!\left[\{N_Bv-h^{\mathsf T}G^+b\}^2\mid X\right]
=E\{(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\mid X\}. \tag{31}
\]
Thus the positive-probability rank increase is equivalent to \(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi\ne0\) in \(L^2(P)\).

Because \(Q\) is an orthogonal projection and \((I-Q)\phi=\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\), the two parts are orthogonal.  Therefore, for every \(c\in\mathbb R^K\),
\[
c^{\mathsf T}(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}})c
=E\{(c^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\}. \tag{32}
\]
Combining (31)--(32) gives the advertised observable certificate and strict adjacent-step gain exactly when \(P_X(\Lambda_j>0)>0\).

On the half-margin fit set, \(D,\widehat D\) and \(H=B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B,\widehat H=\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\) have inverse norms bounded by a constant depending only on the regular margins.  The identities
\[
\widehat D^{-1}-D^{-1}=\widehat D^{-1}(D-\widehat D)D^{-1},
\qquad
\widehat H^{-1}-H^{-1}=\widehat H^{-1}(H-\widehat H)H^{-1} \tag{33}
\]
and product telescoping yield pointwise
\[
\|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}). \tag{34}
\]
Taking the declared conditional \(L^2\) norm proves the first assertion.

For the possibly singular Gram matrices, fixed equal rank and the nonzero spectral gap give the algebraic pseudoinverse difference identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat G^+-G^+
={}&-\widehat G^+(\widehat G-G)G^+
+\widehat G^{+2}(\widehat G-G)(I-GG^+)\\
&+(I-\widehat G^+\widehat G)(\widehat G-G)G^{+2}.
\end{aligned} \tag{35}
\]
Multiplication by the four Penrose equations verifies (35).  Every pseudoinverse in (35) has norm at most \(2/\varepsilon\), so \(\|\widehat G^+-G^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

Apply (33)--(35), the two bridge inverse identities, and product telescoping successively to \(R,N,c,h,G,b\).  Bounded \(Y\), the half-margin constraints, and finite \(K\) make every untouched factor uniformly bounded.  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz then gives
\[
\|\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G^+\widehat b_{\widehat U}
-h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\|_2
\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma,
\qquad
\|\widehat N\widehat U-N_BU\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{36}
\]
Their difference is the asserted correction bound.  The same inverse identities applied to the product bridge give \(\|\widehat U-U\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma\); combining this with (36) proves stability of the full efficient score.  The displayed bound for the sum of the derived rates follows from these same telescoping inequalities (and is also bounded by the defining aggregate \(R_\Sigma\)).

Fix a target coordinate and put \(k=QU\), \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\).  Both terms defining \(\widehat k\) lie in \(\operatorname{range}(\widehat N)=\ker(\widehat B^{\mathsf T})\), so \(\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat k=0\) pointwise.  Since \(d=Bw\), conditioning on \(X\) gives
\[
E_P(\widehat k\mid X)
=\int g(y\mid X)\sum_{j=1}^Kw_j(y,X)(B_{\cdot j}-\widehat B_{\cdot j})^{\mathsf T}\widehat k(y,X)d\nu(y). \tag{37}
\]
Write \(\Delta_A=M_A-\widehat M_A\) and \(\Delta_Z=M_Z-\widehat M_Z\).  Exactly,
\[
B_{\cdot j}-\widehat B_{\cdot j}
=\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes M_{Z,\cdot j}
+M_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}
-\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}. \tag{38}
\]
The first term in (38), paired with the true \(k\), integrates to
\[
\pi_j\sum_a\Delta_{A,aj}
 \int f_j(y\mid X)\sum_zM_{Z,zj}k_{az}(y,X)d\nu(y)=0, \tag{39}
\]
because \(E(k\mid A,J,X)=0\); when \(M_{A,aj}=0\), the same-support fit has \(\Delta_{A,aj}=0\).  The second linear term vanishes analogously using \(E(k\mid Z,J,X)=0\).  Substitute \(\widehat k-k\) in those two terms and retain \(\widehat k\) in the product term.  Uniform bounds and conditional Cauchy--Schwarz, followed by Lemma 6, give
\[
\|E_P\widehat k\|
\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{(r_A+r_Z)\|\widehat k-k\|_2+r_Ar_Z\}
\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{(r_A+r_Z)R_\Sigma+r_Ar_Z\}. \tag{40}
\]

For the raw bridge define
\[
\delta^A_{j\ell}=E\{\widehat a_j(A,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\},
\qquad \delta^Z_{j\ell}=E\{\widehat z_j(Z,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\]
Direct conditioning under three-view independence gives the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
E(\widehat U_j\mid X)-m_j
={}&(\widehat m_j-m_j)
\left[1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}(1+\delta^A_{jj})(1+\delta^Z_{jj})\right]\\
&+\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\sum_{\ell\ne j}\pi_\ell
\delta^A_{j\ell}\delta^Z_{j\ell}(m_\ell-\widehat m_j). 
\end{aligned} \tag{41}
\]
The bridge inverse identity and the half-margin bounds imply \(\|\delta^A\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A\) and \(\|\delta^Z\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z\).  Cauchy--Schwarz in (41) therefore yields
\[
\|E_P\widehat U-\psi\|
\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)+r_Ar_Z\}. \tag{42}
\]
Since the estimated efficient score is \(\widehat U-\widehat k\), (40)--(42) prove the stated \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n\) bound.  If only \(M_A\) is perturbed, (42) has no linear term and (40) is quadratic; if only \(f\) is perturbed, \(B=\widehat B\), so (37) is exactly zero and (41) is exactly unbiased.  This proves the asserted first-order cancellations.

Let \(S(O)=U(O)-QU(O)=\psi+\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O)\), and on fold \(f\) let \(\widehat S_f=\widehat U_f-\widehat Q_f\widehat U_f\).  Add and subtract foldwise conditional means to obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)
={}&n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}\sum_{i:\,\mathrm{fold}(i)=f}
\bigl[(\widehat S_f-S)(O_i)-P(\widehat S_f-S)\bigr]\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}n_fP(\widehat S_f-\psi). 
\end{aligned} \tag{43}
\]
Conditional on each training sample, the middle line has variance at most a fixed-fold constant times \(\|\widehat S_f-S\|_2^2\).  Lemma 6 and \(R_\Sigma=o_P(1)\), followed by conditional Chebyshev, make it \(o_P(1)\).  Lemma 7 bounds the norm of the last line by \(\sqrt n\,C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n=o_P(1)\).  This proves the asymptotic linear expansion.

The influence function is bounded on the regular stratum.  For any fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^K\), a second-order Taylor expansion of its characteristic function gives
\[
E\exp\{it^{\mathsf T}\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}/\sqrt n\}
=1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}),
\]
uniformly for fixed \(t\).  Independence raises this expression to the \(n\)-th power, whose limit is \(\exp\{-t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t/2\}\).  Thus the leading vector in (43) converges to \(N(0,V_{\mathrm{eff}})\), and the same holds for the estimator.

Finally, Lemma 6 gives foldwise \(L^2\) convergence of the estimated scores to \(S\).  Conditional laws of large numbers on the held-out folds, finite-fold summation, and \(\widehat\psi\to_P\psi\) show that their centered empirical second moment converges to \(E\{(S-\psi)(S-\psi)^{\mathsf T}\}=V_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  Hence \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{eff}}\).

Multiplying the expansion in Theorem 8 by the fixed matrix \(C\) gives
\[
\sqrt n(C\widehat\psi-C\psi)
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nC\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1)
\rightsquigarrow N(0,CV_{\mathrm{eff}}C^{\mathsf T}). \tag{44}
\]
Consistency of \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) and continuity of matrix multiplication give \(\widehat\Sigma_C\to_P\Sigma_C\).  Positive definiteness makes every diagonal variance positive and makes standardization continuous in a neighborhood of \(\Sigma_C\).

Let \(R_C\) and \(\widehat R_C\) be the correlation matrices obtained from \(\Sigma_C\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_C\).  Then \(\widehat R_C\to_PR_C\).  For fixed \(q\), the distribution of \(\max_{r\leq q}|Z_r|\), \(Z\sim N(0,R_C)\), is continuous because every coordinate has a continuous marginal and the boundary of a rectangle has Gaussian probability zero.  Therefore its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile evaluated at \(\widehat R_C\) converges to the true quantile.  Applying this fact to (44) and the consistent coordinate standard errors proves simultaneous coverage tending to \(1-\alpha\).  The centering condition \(C\mathbf 1_K=0\) makes all rows treatment contrasts, while full row rank and positive information exclude redundant or zero-variance reported coordinates.

In the binary restriction write \(\mu_{Aj}=E(A\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}}=j,X)\) and \(\mu_{Zj}=E(Z\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}}=j,X)\).  At fixed \((y,x)\), the two cell vectors
\[
B_0=(A-\mu_{A0})(Z-\mu_{Z1}),\qquad
B_1=(A-\mu_{A1})(Z-\mu_{Z0})
\]
satisfy \(B^{\mathsf T}B_0=B^{\mathsf T}B_1=0\): for each latent class, one of the two centered factors has conditional mean zero, and conditional independence factors the expectation.  The binary \(B\) has rank two, so \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\) has dimension two.  Measurement separation makes \(B_0,B_1\) linearly independent, hence every outcome-null cell function is uniquely
\[
k=B_0h_0(Y,X)+B_1h_1(Y,X). \tag{45}
\]
The restrictions conditional on \((A,J,X)\) applied successively at \(J=0,1\) imply \(E(h_0\mid J=0,X)=E(h_1\mid J=1,X)=0\); the restrictions conditional on \((Z,J,X)\) imply the two crossed equations.  Thus
\[
E(h_r\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}},X)=0,\qquad r=0,1. \tag{46}
\]
Conversely (46) makes all three conditional restrictions vanish.  The first \(D\)-orthogonal projection \(N_B\) removes the two-dimensional column space of \(B\); residualizing the four binary measurement representers and solving their conditional Gram system removes exactly the remaining violations of (46).  The same normal-equation calculation as (23)--(24), now wholly inside the binary restriction, therefore shows that \(Q\) is the orthogonal projection onto the space generated by (45)--(46).  This proves the Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen continuous binary reduction without invoking the \(K\geq3\) theorem.

If \(Y\) is binary, each \(h_r(Y,X)\) has two cell values.  The two equations in (46) have coefficient matrix formed by the two distinct class-conditional Bernoulli laws; the binary outcome-feature rank makes it nonsingular.  Hence \(h_0=h_1=0\), \(\operatorname{range}Q=\{0\}\), and \(Q\phi=0\).  This is only a restriction check and changes neither the \(K\ge3\) assumptions nor theorem scope.

All entries in the definition of \(P^\star\) are rational.  The three class means are
\[
m=\left(\frac9{10},\frac32,\frac{21}{10}\right)^{\mathsf T},
\]
because the conditional mean within bin \(b\) is \(b+1/2\).  The density entries lie in \([1/10,7/10]\), so common support and the density envelope for \(\varepsilon=3/1000\) hold; also \(|Y|\le3\).  The singular values of \(M_A\) are \(1,7/10,7/10\), those of \(M_Z\) are \(1,2/5,2/5\), and those of \(H=\Gamma_Y\) are \(1,3/5,2/5\).  The modal gap is \(7/10\), and \(\min_j\pi_j=3/10\).

For each of the three outcome bins, form exactly
\[
B_{(a,z),j}=M_{A,aj}M_{Z,zj},\quad
w_j=\frac{\pi_jH_{bj}}{\sum_\ell\pi_\ell H_{b\ell}},\quad
D=\operatorname{diag}(Bw),\quad R=D^{-1}BW. \tag{47}
\]
Exact rational evaluation of (47) gives \(\min_{b,a,z}d_{az}=69/1600>3/1000\).  Direct rational characteristic-polynomial sign counts give, in every bin,
\[
\lambda_{\min}(R^{\mathsf T}DR)\in(38349/10^6,38350/10^6). \tag{48}
\]
Constructing \(h\) and summing its three rational bin contributions gives a rational \(18\times18\) matrix \(G\).  Exact row reduction has twelve pivots and six zero rows, while successive exact sign counts for its rational characteristic polynomial place the twelve nonzero roots in
\[
\begin{gathered}
(3413/10^6,3414/10^6),\ (3658/10^6,3659/10^6),\\
(5796/10^6,5797/10^6),\ (7974/10^6,7975/10^6),\\
(9442/10^6,9443/10^6),\ (14792/10^6,14793/10^6),\\
(33245/10^6,33246/10^6),\ (38068/10^6,38069/10^6),\\
(46032/10^6,46033/10^6),\ (69133/10^6,69134/10^6),\\
(91140/10^6,91141/10^6),\ (113149/10^6,113150/10^6).
\end{gathered} \tag{49}
\]
All twelve intervals are positive.  In particular \(\operatorname{rank}G=12\) and its least nonzero eigenvalue exceeds \(3/1000\).  Equations (47)--(49), together with the already verified causal construction, prove \(P^\star\in\mathcal M_{3,0.003}\).  All inequalities are strict; bounded exponential tilts of the positive factors preserve them for sufficiently small positive and negative parameters, so \(P^\star\) is a two-sided pathwise-interior point.

On each bin, \(R,D,N,h\) are constant and \(\phi\) is affine in \(u=y-b\in[0,1]\).  Therefore every covariance integral is exactly obtained from \(\int_0^1(1,u,u^2)du=(1,1/2,1/3)\).  Carrying out these rational operations gives
\[
V_{\mathrm{raw}}=
\begin{pmatrix}
67699/8820&2927/7840&5689/13230\\
2927/7840&1357/294&2927/7840\\
5689/13230&2927/7840&67699/8820
\end{pmatrix}. \tag{50}
\]
For \(K_0=Q\phi\), the same calculation verifies
\[
V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}=E(K_0K_0^{\mathsf T}). \tag{51}
\]
Exact rational Gaussian elimination places the three leading principal minors of (51), respectively, in
\[
(1114/1000,1115/1000),\qquad(1219/1000,1220/1000),
\qquad(1199/1000,1200/1000). \tag{52}
\]
They are positive, so (51) is positive definite.  Thus \(Q\phi\ne0\).  Theorem 4 applies at this interior witness and yields \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\in\mathcal T\).  Equations (47), (49), and the definition of \(Q\) show directly that evaluation uses nine cells and one Gram solve of dimension eighteen, completing every assertion.

theorem.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the corrected handle \(\mathfrak I\) admits a measurable uniformly bounded right inverse on every observed-data DQM score: if \(s\in L^2_0(P)\) is the score of an observed path through \(P\), there are factorwise centered scores \(s_X,s_\pi,s_Y,s_A,s_Z\) such that
\[
s=E_P\{s_X(X)+s_\pi(J,X)+s_Y(Y,J,X)+s_A(A,J,X)+s_Z(Z,J,X)\mid O\},
\]
and the sum of their factor \(L^2\)-norms is at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\|s\|_{L^2(P)}\).  The recovery is measurable in \(X\), uses the augmented finite-feature inverse to fix the differentiated factorization, then uses the conditional \(G(X)^+\) solve for the measurement scores and the pointwise \(\{R^{\mathsf T}DR\}^{-1}\) solve for the remaining mixture and class-density scores.  Class-density scores are support preserving.
theorem.proof_tex:
Let \(s\) be the score of an observed DQM path and put \(s_X=E_P(s\mid X)\) and \(s_c=s-s_X\).  Conditional DQM differentiation gives a conditional cell-density derivative \(\dot p_r(y\mid x)=p_r(y\mid x)s_c(y,r,x)\), where \(r=(a,z)\).  The augmented finite moments are bounded functions of \(O\); hence their derivatives are conditional expectations of those functions times \(s_c\).  Conditional Jensen's inequality and Lemma 2A give measurable derivatives of \(\pi,M_A,M_Z,\Gamma_Y\) with conditional squared norm bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2E(s_c^2\mid X)\).  This also fixes the locally constant modal labeling.

Differentiate the product factorization.  On supported atoms its formal conditional-score identity is
\[
s_c(y,a,z,x)=\sum_{j=1}^KR_{(a,z),j}(y,x)
 \{s_{\pi,j}(x)+s_{Y,j}(y,x)+s_{A,aj}(x)+s_{Z,zj}(x)\}. \tag{10}
\]
At a zero factor atom a two-sided probability derivative is zero, so the corresponding score may be set to zero.  Although the initially differentiated measurement scores need not yet have a useful uniform norm, (10) is an algebraic identity.

Let \(u\in\mathbb R^{2K^2}\) collect the \(s_A\) and \(s_Z\) coordinates.  Terms in (10) depending only on \((Y,J,X)\) have cell vector in \(\operatorname{range}(R)=\ker(N_B)\).  The measurement term is \(c^{\mathsf T}u\).  Therefore
\[
N_Bs_c=h^{\mathsf T}u. \tag{11}
\]
Taking conditional inner products with \(h\) gives
\[
b_s(X):=E\{hN_Bs_c\mid X\}=G(X)u. \tag{12}
\]
On the \(2K(K-1)\)-dimensional subspace on which every \(A\)- and \(Z\)-block is factorwise centered, the map \(u\mapsto h^{\mathsf T}u\) is injective.  Indeed, if it vanished, then \(c^{\mathsf T}u\in\operatorname{range}R\); subtracting that \(R\)-term would give a zero observed derivative with a nonzero normalized measurement derivative, contradicting the injectivity calculation of Lemma 2A after taking the finite feature moments.  Hence \(\operatorname{rank}G=2K(K-1)\); its remaining \(2K\) null directions are precisely the blockwise constants used below.

Every vector in \(\ker G(X)\) has zero inner product with \(h\) conditionally, so \(b_s(X)\in\operatorname{range}G(X)\).  Choose \(u_0=G^+b_s\).  The nonzero-spectrum gap yields
\[
\|u_0(X)\|_2^2\leq\varepsilon^{-1}E\{(N_Bs_c)^2\mid X\}. \tag{13}
\]
Subtracting from each \(A\)-block its \(M_A(\cdot\mid j,X)\)-mean, and analogously for \(Z\), centers \(u_0\).  Such blockwise constants are annihilated by \(N_Bc\), because their cell image is a linear combination of the columns of \(R\).  Thus centering preserves (11), and, since all weights are at most one and \(K\) is fixed, changes the right side of (13) by at most a constant depending on \(K\).  Call the centered coordinates \(s_A,s_Z\).

Set \(s_0=s_c-c^{\mathsf T}u\).  Equation (11) gives \(N_Bs_0=0\).  Lemma 3A gives \(\ker N_B=\operatorname{range}R\), so, pointwise,
\[
t(y,x)=\{R^{\mathsf T}DR\}^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}Ds_0(y,\cdot,x),
\qquad s_0=Rt. \tag{14}
\]
The posterior Gram gap and the identity \(s_0=Rt\) imply
\[
\int g(y\mid x)\sum_jw_j(y,x)t_j(y,x)^2d\nu(y)
 \leq\varepsilon^{-1}E(s_0^2\mid X=x). \tag{15}
\]
Define
\[
s_{\pi,j}(x)=\int f_j(y\mid x)t_j(y,x)d\nu(y),
\qquad s_{Y,j}(y,x)=t_j(y,x)-s_{\pi,j}(x). \tag{16}
\]
Then \(E(s_Y\mid J,X)=0\).  The measurement scores are factorwise centered, and \(E(s_c\mid X)=0\), so (14) also gives \(\sum_j\pi_js_{\pi,j}=0\).  Thus all scores in (10) have the required conditional centering.  Equations (10)--(16) give the requested right inverse.  Bounds (13)--(15), the uniform Euclidean bound on \(N_B\) from cell positivity, and conditional Jensen give the asserted global \(L^2\) bound.

All displayed inverses and pseudoinverses are Borel measurable on their fixed-rank strata.  Finally, common support gives \(f_j>0\) \(\nu\)-almost everywhere.  Equation (16) is a class-density score with \(\int f_js_{Y,j}d\nu=0\); the bounded truncations \(s_{Y,j}^{(M)}\), recentered under \(f_j\), generate positive normalized exponential-tilt paths and converge in class-factor \(L^2\).  This proves support-preserving recovery and completes the handle.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the observable augmented moment system
\[
 S(x)=\{P(A=a,Z=z\mid X=x)\}_{a,z},\qquad
 T_u(x)=E_P\{h_{0,u}(Y)e_Ae_Z^{\mathsf T}\mid X=x\},\quad u=1,\ldots,K,
\]
identifies \((\pi,M_A,M_Z,\Gamma_Y)\), and hence \((\pi,M_A,M_Z,f)\), up to a common permutation.  The modal margin selects the unique ordered labeling, and \(\psi_j=E_P\{m_j(X)\}=E\{Y(j)\}\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The feature tensor alone identifies the product of each mixing weight and outcome-feature column, not those two factors separately.  Adding the observed normalization slice \(P(A,Z\mid X)\), which is already part of the observed law, removes this scaling ambiguity.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\) under which \(X\) is degenerate, the derivative of the augmented normalized moment map \((S,T_1,\ldots,T_K)\), with \(S=P(A,Z)\) and \(T_u=E\{h_{0,u}(Y)e_Ae_Z^{\mathsf T}\}\), has a right inverse on its observed finite-feature score image whose operator norm is bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  Applying the corrected \(\mathfrak I_0\) recovers centered derivatives, and hence centered scores, for \(\pi\), \(M_A\), \(M_Z\), and \(\Gamma_Y\) under the modal labeling.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The derivative is injective only for the augmented moment map containing the observed \((A,Z)\) marginal; the unaugmented feature tensor retains a mixing-weight/outcome-feature scaling kernel.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
At every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), meaning that every bounded factorwise centered additive latent score generates for all sufficiently small positive and negative path parameters a product-factor path remaining in \(\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the full observed-data tangent space satisfies \(\mathcal T=\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}^{\,L^2(P)}\).  At such a \(P\),
\[
\mathcal T^{\perp}=\{k\in L^2_0(P):E(k\mid Y,J,X)=E(k\mid A,J,X)=E(k\mid Z,J,X)=0\}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The class is defined by closed inequality constraints.  At an active boundary, its DQM tangent span need not contain every latent factor score appearing in the unrestricted class \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\).  The reverse inclusion is valid at the explicitly defined two-sided pathwise-interior points; the difficult inclusion of every observed score into \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is proved without this restriction.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the outcome-score restrictions \(E_P(k\mid Y,J=j,X)=0\) are equivalent, cellwise, to \(B^{\mathsf T}k=0\).  The operator \(N=N_B=I_{K^2}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) is their pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector, \(b_{f_0}(X)\in\operatorname{range}\{G(X)\}\), and \(Qf_0=N_Bf_0-h^{\mathsf T}G(X)^+b_{f_0}(X)\) is the \(L^2(P)\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal T^\perp\) for every \(f_0\in L^2(P)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The cell and Gram algebra is valid throughout the regular class, but its identification with the orthocomplement of the full model tangent space uses the corrected pathwise-interior tangent-completeness theorem.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: At every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\) and every fixed \(K\geq3\), the vector \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi-Q\phi\), with first elimination \(N_B=I_{K^2}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\), is the unique canonical gradient for \(\psi\), and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) is the semiparametric efficiency bound.  The operator uses fixed \(K^2\)-cell algebra and one Gram solve of dimension at most \(2K^2\), with no outcome-partition resolution or outcome-basis approximation index.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Canonicality relative to the full inequality-defined model follows from tangent completeness only at two-sided pathwise-interior points.  The projection formula itself remains well defined on the whole regular stratum.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every regular coherent foldwise fit constrained as in the corrected definition, measure a pointwise matrix error by its conditional \(L^2(P)\) norm.  Then
\[
\{E_P\|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}^{1/2}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_D+r_B),
\]
\(r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b=O_P(R_\Sigma)\), and
\[
\|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_{L^2(P)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
\]
The full estimated efficient score \(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U\) has the same linear \(L^2(P)\) stability bound relative to \(U-QU\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original pointwise operator-norm inequality was not well typed against integrated nuisance errors.  The corrected claim uses the conditional \(L^2\) norm of the pointwise operator error and makes the regular fitted-rank event explicit.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Use \(\mathfrak I_0\): when \(X\) is degenerate, augment the \(K\times K\times K\) feature tensor \(T_u=E\{h_{0,u}(Y)e_Ae_Z^{\mathsf T}\}\) by the observed normalization slice \(S=P(A,Z)\), differentiate \((S,T_1,\ldots,T_K)\), and invert its separated finite Jacobian on the observed score image to recover centered scores for \(\pi\), \(M_A\), \(M_Z\), and \(\Gamma_Y\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The observed \((A,Z)\) marginal is the normalization slice that separates the mixing weights from the outcome-feature columns; omitting it leaves a \((K-1)\)-dimensional scaling ambiguity.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For each training fold, fit one label-aligned product factorization represented by \(\widehat\eta\), constrained to the declared common support and to the half-margin regular set: \(\widehat\pi_j\geq\varepsilon/2\), \(\widehat d_{az}\geq\varepsilon/2\), the relevant measurement and posterior least singular values are at least \(\varepsilon/2\), and \(\widehat G\) has the structural rank \(2K(K-1)\) with every nonzero eigenvalue at least \(\varepsilon/2\).  Set \(\widehat W=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat w)\), \(\widehat B=\widehat M_A\odot\widehat M_Z\), \(\widehat d=\widehat B\widehat w\), \(\widehat D=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat d)\), \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), \(\widehat N=I_{K^2}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B(\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^+\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\), \(\widehat h=\widehat N\widehat c\), and derive \(\widehat G\), \(\widehat b_{(\cdot)}\), \(\widehat b_U\), and \(\widehat Q\) from those same objects before held-out evaluation.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The original construction uses ordinary matrix inverses and fixed-rank pseudoinverses without requiring fitted objects to remain on their domain.  Constraining each fit to the feasible half-margin set makes every displayed score and stability bound well defined.

proposed.statement: In the binary restriction \(J^{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\mathcal I^\ell\), \(\mathcal Q^\ell\), \(\mathcal P_1^\ell\), the nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions \(p_1^\ell,\ldots,p_{\ell-2}^\ell\), and \(V^\ell=(B_0p_1^\ell,B_1p_1^\ell,\ldots,B_0p_{\ell-2}^\ell,B_1p_{\ell-2}^\ell)^{\mathsf T}\) be exactly the outcome-partition construction of Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen Supplement S8.2.  With \(Q\) built from the corrected \(D\)-orthogonal first elimination \(N_B\), every well-defined \(\operatorname{span}(V^\ell)\) is contained in \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\), and \(V_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}=E_P[\{(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}\{(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}^{\mathsf T}]\succeq0\).  The gap is strict in a contrast direction \(c\) exactly when \(c^{\mathsf T}(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\neq0\).  Along a nested equal-width refinement subsequence, the Supplement S8.2 density of \(\mathcal P_1^\ell\) in the binary conditional-null space implies \(Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\phi\to Q\phi\) in \(L^2(P)\) and \(V_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\to V_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  This comparison is a binary restriction only; the exact fixed-cell theorem is asserted for \(K\geq3\).

proposed.statement: For every coherent foldwise fit using \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\) and the corrected \(\widehat N\), \(\|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n\), where \(\Delta_n=r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)+r_Ar_Z+(r_A+r_Z)R_\Sigma\); in particular, perturbing only \(M_A\) or only \(f\) has zero first-order mean bias.
proposed.justification: The cancellation shows that the finite efficiency correction preserves orthogonality when all fitted objects arise from one product law.
proposed.gap: The projected correction adds posterior and Gram errors, whose mean is controlled by the finite-projector conditional-zero equations.
proposed.consumer: It permits flexible learning of exposure misclassification and birth-weight regressions under explicit product-rate conditions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A proof that the specifically prescribed global tensor-product B-spline product-likelihood fit and empirical-minimum label rule attain the four primitive factor rates uniformly enough to stay in the fixed-rank half-margin set.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen assumptions specify Hölder membership but do not specify the spline boundary/extension convention on the general outcome support, the constrained likelihood parameterization, a local likelihood-curvature inequality, or the uniform-norm control needed by the minimum-over-training-points label selector.  Those facts do not follow from the finite projector algebra.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced all derived nuisance rates to the four primitive rates by inverse identities and fixed-rank pseudoinverse perturbation; checked that \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\) makes the resulting squared rate negligible at root \(n\).  A direct sieve-likelihood proof stops at the missing curvature and uniform label-selection premises.
open_obligations.partial_result: The regular-stratum algebra does prove the following propagation statement: if one constrained, label-aligned primitive fit satisfies \(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z+r_f=O_P(\rho_n)\), then bounded integration gives \(r_m=O_P(\rho_n)\), and the inverse, Bayes, projector, and fixed-rank pseudoinverse identities give every derived coordinate \(r_w,r_W,r_B,r_d,r_D,r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b=O_P(\rho_n)\).  Consequently \(R_\Sigma=O_P(\rho_n)\) and \(\Delta_n=O_P(\rho_n^2)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) when \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\).  What is not proved from the frozen primitives is that the specifically named product-likelihood B-spline fit, with the empirical-minimum permutation rule, attains the four primitive rates without additional likelihood curvature, spline-domain, and uniform label-selection conditions.
